3400:
** μῑλῐ-ον**, τό,
**a Roman mile**, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 34.11.8, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.1.9, NT.Matt.5.41, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “C. Gracchus” 7}}:—also **μείλιον** (which see).
3404:
** μῑσ-έω**,
_perfect_ μεμίσηκα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 44c}}:—_passive_, _future_ _middle_ in _passive_ sense μισήσομαι {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 664, “Ion” 597, 611, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 6.13, later μισηθήσομαι LXX.Sir.21.28, 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 2.426 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 52.39}}: _aorist_ ἐμισήθην {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.119, etc.}}: _perfect_ μεμίσημαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.137, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 8.5.8}}: (μῖσος):—**hate**, once in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, with _accusative_ et}}_infinitive_, μίσησεν δ᾽ ἄρα μιν δηΐων κυσὶ κύρμα γενέσθαι Zeus **hated (would not suffer**) that he should become a prey.., {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.272; μισῶ φίλοισιν ὕστερον βοηδρομεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 333}}; οὐ μισοῦντ᾽ ἐκείνην τὴν πόλιν, τὸ μὴ οὐ μεγάλην εἶναι not **hating** that city, as not being.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 36}}; μισῶ λακωνίζειν I **hate** Laconizing, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 351.1}}: but mostly with _accusative_, ὑβρίζοντα μισεῖν {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.284; μισοῦντ᾽ ἐμίσει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1134, etc.; θεῖον μισεῖ μῖσος.. με 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 216; μ. τινὰ μῖσος ἐξαίσιον 5th c.AD: Aristaenetus Rhetor 1.22; ὃ μισεῖς μηδενὶ ποιήσῃς LXX.Tob.4.15}}:—_passive_, **to be hated**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same place], etc.; ὦ πολλὰ μισηθεῖσα χειρωναξία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 45, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 818; μισεῖσθαι ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.83; μισηθεὶς ἔσχατον μῖσος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 6.}}

3414:
** μνᾶ**, ἡ,
_genitive_ μνᾶς, _nominative_ _plural_ μναῖ, etc., always contracted in _Attic dialect_, as {{Refs|“IG” 12.10.3, 22.1627.299, etc.}}; _Ionic dialect_ _nominative_ _plural_ μνέαι {{Refs 6th c.BC+|“Schwyzer” 707 (Ephesus, 6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.168, 6.79}}; _accusative_ _plural_ μνέας {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Schwyzer” [same place], 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149, 180, +others, μνέ[ας] “IG” 12(5).123b (from Paros)}}; but _accusative_ _singular_ μνῆν {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.51; _genitive_ μνῆς [prev. author] 7.91; _genitive_ _plural_ μνέων [prev. author] 2.22}}; _nominative_ _plural_ μνέες _falsa lectio_ for{μνέαι} in {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Syr.D.” 48}}:—**mina**,
**I** as **a weight**, = {{Refs 4th c.BC+|100 drachmae, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.76, etc., compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 9.59, 86.}}
**II** as **a sum of money**, also = {{Refs 5th c.BC+|100 drachmae, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.63, etc.}} (Semitic word, cf. Hebrew **māneh.**)

3425:
** μόγῐς**,
_Aeolic dialect_ **μύγις** {{Refs 6th c.AD+|6th c.AD: Joannes Alexandrinus Grammaticus “Comp.” 3.10}}: _adverb_, (μόγος) **with toil and pain**, i. e. **hardly, scarcely**, {{NT+8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.355, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.119, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.116, NT.Luke.9.39, etc.; μ. ἀνεκτοί 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.10; μ. παρειποῦσ᾽ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 131 (Lyric poetry); μ. πολλῷ πόνῳ [prev. author] “Pers.” 509; τὸν μ. Ἀττικόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 31; πάνυ μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 360d; μ. πως [prev. author] “Chrm.” 155e; μ. καὶ κατ᾽ ὀλίγον 2nd c.AD(?): Charito Scriptor Eroticus 1.8; βίᾳ καὶ μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 108b.—Cf. the post- 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus μόλις: μόλις}} is rare in _Attic dialect_ Prose, except in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, where it is commoner than μόλις}}; both forms in codices of {{Refs 8th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus [ῑ for the sake of meter, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.412.]}}
3430:
** μοιχ-εία**, ἡ,
**adultery**, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.10, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.36, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 443a (_plural_); μοιχείας γραφαί 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc., 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see at {πέμπτῃ φθίνοντος}.}}]
3433:
** μόλῐς**,
_adverb_, post-{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus synonym of μόγις}}, prevailing in Trag., Comedy texts, and _Attic dialect_ prose, though in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus and later prose μόγις was preferred (in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus}} the Laur. Ms. gives each form twice, the same Ms. of {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus μόλις always)}}; μ. μέν, ἀλλ᾽ ὅμως ἠνεσχόμην {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1363, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 290, 1105, “El.” 575, “Ph.” 329}}; ζῶντι καὶ μάλα μ. nay, **only just** alive, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142b (codex W μόγις)}}; μ. καὶ ἠρέμα πάσχειν **scarcely at all**.., {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1019a31 (codex Ab μόγις); ἢ ὅλως οὐκ ἔστιν ἢ μ. [prev. author] “Ph.” 217b32; μ. πάνυ 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 30; πάνυ μ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 88.8: with a _negative_, οὐ μ.}} **not scarcely**, i.e. **quite, utterly**, ἀπώλεσας οὐ μ. {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1082; θυραῖος ἔστω πόλεμος, οὐ μ. παρών [prev. author] “Eu.” 864 (where Scholia explains οὐ μ. by οὐ μακράν, but the sense is uncertain)}}; θέλουσαν οὐ μ. καλεῖς {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 334 (Lyric poetry).}}

3437:
** μομφή**, ἡ,
_poetry_ form of μέμψις (also in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 323b)}}, **blame, reproof**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.39; μομφῆς ἄτερ τέθνηκεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1015}}; **cause of complaint**, μομφὰν ἔχειν τινί {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).36}}; ἕν σοι μομφὴν ἔχω in one thing I **blame** thee, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1069; μομφὰς ὑπὸ σπλάγχνοις ἔχειν [prev. author] Alcaeus1009; πρός τινα μ. ἔχειν NT.Col.3.13: with _genitive_, μ. ἔχων ξυνοῦ δορός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 180 (Lyric poetry); ὧν ἕνεκα μ. ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 664.}}
3442:
** μον-όφθαλμος**,
_Ionic dialect_ **μουν-**, ον, **one-eyed**, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.116, 4.27, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.9, NT.Matt.18.9: rejected by 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 112}}; explained as **one who has one eye**, like the Cyclops, opposed to ἑτερόφθαλμος, **one who has lost an eye**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Ammonius Grammaticus “περὶ ὁμοίων καὶ διαφόρων λέξεων” p.60 V.}}
3445:
** μορφ-όω**,
**give shape** or **form to**, γυναικῶν σώματα μορφώσαντες καὶ ὁπλίσαντες ὡς ἐς ἄνδρας μάλιστα {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 40.4, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 375}}:—_passive_, **receive shape** or **form**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 5.6.7, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1013c, etc.; ἄχρις οὗ μορφωθῇ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν NT.Gal.4.19.}}
3449:
** μόχθ-ος**, ὁ,
= Homeric μόγος, **toil, hardship, distress**, ἀμφὶ δ᾽ ἀέθλῳ δῆριν ἔχειν καὶ μ. {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 306}}; μόχθων ἀμπνοά, ἀμοιβά, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.7, “N.” 5.48: frequently in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 921, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 480, etc.}}: also in _plural_, **toils, troubles, hardships**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 541 (Lyric poetry)}}, etc.; of the **labours** of Heracles, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1101, 1170}}; μ. τέκνων **for** them, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1261 (Lyric poetry)}}; μόχθον ἀμφὶ πράγμασι epigram cited in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184}}; Ἀπελλείου μ. γραφίδος, of a picture, {{NT+5th c.BC+|“APl.” 4.178 (Antip. Sid.).—Rare in early Prose (not in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus or Oratt.), compare μ. καὶ ταλαιπωρίη 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 223; ἐλευθέριοι μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.4; διὰ μόχθων [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.6.25: frequently in LXX, LXX.Exo.18.8, +others; κόπος καὶ μ. NT.1Thes.2.9}}; μ. implies **hardship**, πόνος **work** (but μ. is said to be Cretan dialect for πόνος {{Refs|“Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 1096).}}
3459:
** μῠλ-ών**, ῶνος, ὁ,
**mill-house**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.22, “Inscription Délos” 445.22 (2nd c.BC)}}; εἰς μ. καταβαλεῖν to condemn [a slave] to work the **mill**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 240; εἰς μ. ἐμπεσεῖν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.18; ἐν τῷ μ. εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.33, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.23; μ. καὶ πέδαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἥρως” 3; ἄξιοι δεσμωτηρίου καὶ μυλῶνος 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.623}}; Κηφισόδοτος τὰς τριήρεις ἐκάλει μυλῶνας ποικίλους painted **mills**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1411a24. (Sts. _paroxytone_ in codices, as 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus [same place], 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus [same place], 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Vit.Auct.” 27, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.19, but compare 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus Gr. 1.30.)}}

3468:
** μώλωψ**, ωπος, ὁ,
**mark of a stripe, weal, bruise**, {{LXX+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 200, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 889b10, LXX.Isa.53.5, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 16.5, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.565b, etc.}}; of an eruption resembling mosquito bites, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Herodotus Medicus cited in 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 5.129}}; **blood-clot**, {{Refs 7th c.AD+|7th c.AD: Paulus Aegineta Medicus 6.8 (_plural_)}}; πορφύρεοι μώλωπες, satirically of kings, Daphit. cited in {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.1.39.}}
3469:
** μωμ-άομαι**,
_Ionic dialect_ **μωμ-έομαι**, _3rd.pers._ _plural_ -εῦνται {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 369, compare 169}}; _infinitive_ -έεσθαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τέχνης” 1}}: _future_ -ήσομαι {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.412, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1079}}; _Doric dialect_ μωμάσομαι {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.5}}: _aorist_ ἐμωμησάμην {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 277}}; _Doric dialect_ _poetry_ μωμάσατο {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 9.24}}: (μῶμος):—**find fault with, blame, criticize**, with _accusative_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [same place], 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 169, 369, 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus [same place], 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus [same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 171, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 222}}:—_poetry_, _Ionic dialect_ {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|(3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 48, 4th c.AD: Eusebius Myndius Philosophus 1), and later Prose, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 33, +others:}}_aorist_ μωμηθῆναι in _passive_ sense, {{NT|NT.2Cor.6.3}}; see at {μωκάομαι}.
3472:
** μωρ-ία**,
_Ionic dialect_ -ιη, ἡ, (μῶρος) **folly**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.146; μωρίας πλέως 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1150, compare 745}}; μωρίην ἐπιφέρειν τισί to impute **folly** to them, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.131}}; μωρίαν ὀφλισκάνειν to be charged with it, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 470; ἐδόκει μ. εἶναι ταῦτα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.41}}; μωρίᾳ φιλονικεῖν **foolishly**, {{Refs|[prev. author] 4.64}}; τῆς μ. **what folly**! {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 818, “Ec.” 787; εἰς τοῦτ᾽ ἀφῖχθε μωρίας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.54; πολλὴ μ. τοῦ διανοήματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 818d}}; of illicit love, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 644, “Ion” 545.}}

3488:
** νάρκισσ-ος**, ὁ,
rarely ἡ, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.133}}:— **narcissus**, of various species, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“hymnus ad Cererem” 8, 428, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 683 (Lyric poetry), 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.65}}; **pheasant's eye, Narcissus poeticus**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.8.1, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.158}}; **autumn narcissus, N. serotinus**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.6.9}}; **Narcissus Tazetta, polyanthus narcissus**, Dsc. [prev. cited] (this probably in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus [same place]). (Connected with νάρκη}}, because of its **narcotic** properties, _accusative_ to {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.647b.)}}
3489:
** ναυᾱγ-έω**,
_Ionic dialect_ **ναυηγ-**, _perfect_ νεναυάγηκα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.236 (-ηγ-), 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 76}}: (ναῦς, ἄγνυμι):—**suffer shipwreck**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.24, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.10, etc.: _metaphorically_, of chariots, [prev. author] 61.29}}; of an earthen vessel, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 180}}; of persons, ν. ἐν τοῖς ἰδίοις {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus cited in 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 5.55, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.33 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; ἐν τῷ βίῳ 1st c.AD: Cebes Philosophus 24.2; περὶ τὴν πίστιν NT.1Tim.1.19; χὡ μὲν ἐναυάγει γαίης ἔπι “Anthologia Graeca” 5.208 (3rd c.BC: Posidippus Comicus or 3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus); ναυαγεῖ συμπόσια μὴ τυχόντα παιδαγωγίας ὀρθῆς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.622b.}}
3491:
** ναῦς**, ἡ,
(see. below) **ship,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.}} (but rare in non-literary Hellenistic Greek, once in **NT,** {{NT|NT.Acts.27.41, πλοῖον being generally used)}}; ἐν νήεσσι or ἐν νηυσίν at **the ships,** i.e. in the camp formed by the ships drawn up on shore, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.688, 11.659}}; νῆες μακραί **ships** of war, built long and taper for speed, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.41, etc.}}; opposed to νῆες στρογγύλαι round-built merchant-**ships,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.163, etc.}}; νέες alone, ={τριήρεις}, opposed to πεντηκόντεροι, {{Refs|[prev. author] 8.1}}; νῆες κεναί, i.e. without fighting men in them, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.5}}; ναῦς μακρά collective for μακραί, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 380.}}— _Attic dialect_ _declension_ ναῦς, νεώς, νηΐ, ναῦν, dual _genitive_ νεοῖν, _plural_ νῆες, νεῶν (νηῶν is variant in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.15), ναυσί, ναῦς}}; in later writers, _nominative_ _plural_ ναῦς, _accusative_ _plural_ νῆας, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.13, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.2.4, etc., compare 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 147}}:— _Epic dialect_ **νηῦς**, νηός, νηΐ, νῆα, _plural_ νῆες, νηῶν, νηυσί or νήεσσι, νῆας (but also _genitive_ and _accusative_ _singular_ νεός, νέα [the latter as _monosyllable_ in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.283], _plural_ νέες, νεῶν, νέεσσι, νέας)}}; _Epic dialect_ _genitive_ and _dative_ _plural_ ναῦφι, -φιν, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.794, 16.281, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.498}}; in late _Epic dialect_, _nominative_ νῆυς uncertain reading in {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.104, compare “Etymologicum Magnum” 440.17}}; _accusative_ _singular_ and _plural_ νηῦν, νηῦς, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1358, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.3, Dem. Bith. 4.6: Hdn.Gr. 1.401, 2.675, 553 also gives νεῦς, νεΐ (variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.184), and νευσί (5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 27, “Sammelb.” 5829)}}:—_Ionic dialect_ **νηῦς**, νεός, νηΐ, νέα, _plural_ νέες, νεῶν, νηυσί (νηυσίν epigram in {{Refs 7th c.BC+|“IG” 12(8).683 (Thasos, 6th-5th c.BC)), νέας (but νηός 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus (?) in “PLit.Lond.” 54}}; νηός is frequently in codices of {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, νηῶν 7.160)}}:—_Doric dialect_ **ναῦς** (νᾶς{{Refs 5th c.BC+|Hdn.Gr. 1.400), νᾱός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.185, +others, νᾱΐ [prev. author] “O.” 13.54, +others (νᾷ}} perhaps to be read in {{Refs 7th c.BC+|7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 23 iii 27), ναῦν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.245, “fragment” 234 (νᾶν Hdn.Gr. 1.328, νᾶα 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 16.89); _plural_ νᾶες 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 12.4, +others, ναῶν [prev. author] “P.” 1.74, ναυσί, ναυσίν, [prev. author] “N.” 7.29, “P.” 3.68 (νάεσσι [prev. work] 4.56), νᾶας}} _falsa lectio_ in {{Refs 7th c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.17:—_Aeolic dialect_ _sing._ _genitive_ νᾶος, _dative_ νᾶϊ, _plural_ _dative_ νάεσσι, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 19, 18, 79, _genitive_ νᾱων [prev. author] “Supp.” 12.9, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 5.2:—Trag. commonly use _Doric dialect_ forms in Lyric poetry, _Attic dialect_ in dialogue (but sometimes ναός, ναῶν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 62, “Pers.” 340, etc.)}}; the _Epic dialect_ forms νηός {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 761, νηῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1485, νῆας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 744 (Lyric poetry), νηυσίν [prev. author] “Pers.” 370 (codex M)}} are probably corrupt. (Cf. Sanskrit _naús,_ Latin _nāvis,_ etc.)

3496:
** Νεάπολις** [ᾱ], εως, ἡ,
**new city,** _proper name_ of several cities, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Neapolis”: at first in two words, Νέα πόλις, _genitive_ Νέης πόλιος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.91, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.50}}; later in one, Νεάπολις, _genitive_ Νεαπόλεως {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.5.40, _dative_ Νεαπόλει [prev. author] 1.2.13}}: hence **Νεοπολίτης** [ῑ], ου, ὁ, {{Refs|“IG” 12.191.31, +others}}, later **Νεαπολίτης** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Tab.Heracl.” 1.187, 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 736, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.20.14, etc., compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus cited in 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 9.26.}}
